- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.5) — model tends to ignore downside risk.
- Underestimate prices after sharp upward spikes — model overreacts to momentum, then fails to correct.
- Overshoots in early forecast periods (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — model reacts too aggressively.
- Mean reversion bias: if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overpredicts mid-term (10–20 days) — adjust downward by 1–2% for 10+ day horizons.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative after 3–5 days, model still holds high forecast — delay correction by 2–3 days.
- Avoid extrapolating recent highs — if last 3–5 days are rising, model often overfits to that trend, ignoring underlying volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is consistently negative over last 7 days — model is overly optimistic in downturns.
